summary: Candidate picorv32.v is not the upstream core: it is a simplified two-state ADD-only model with stubbed periphery. It can emit an RVFI record for an ADD-like instruction, but it does not preserve original ADD retirement, ordering, trap/halt semantics, memory handshake, parameterized RV32IMC behavior, or CSR/formal behavior under the original wrapper. Frontend PASS only shows elaboration/syntax, not soundness. The narrow insn_add_ch0 checker may still pass because it samples an ADD at CHECK_CYCLE and assumes spec_valid, but that would not mean the original core is represented.

changes.title: Entire core replaced by ADD-only two-state model
changes.analysis: Candidate comments admit a simplified ADD-only partial model, and the body defines only STATE_FETCH/STATE_EXEC, pc, regfile, instr, and a fetch/execute ADD case. The original body contains the full memory interface, decoder, main state machine, IRQ/PCPI, counters, compressed ISA, and RVFI logic.
changes.property_impact: Under the original wrapper, RVFI no longer reflects original instruction retirement, traps, memory traffic, ordering, CSRs, or compressed/M-extension execution. The ADD checker may be satisfiable, but the candidate is not the original core.
changes.concern: This is a wholesale replacement, not a targeted repair; frontend PASS is not evidence of equivalence.

changes.title: Wrapper parameters ignored by candidate core
changes.analysis: The wrapper enables COMPRESSED_ISA=1, ENABLE_FAST_MUL=1, ENABLE_DIV=1, BARREL_SHIFTER=1. Candidate environment.md states the core ignores all parameters except PROGADDR_RESET, while property_proposal.md claims 'unchanged'. The candidate parameter list is present but unused except for reset PC.
changes.property_impact: RV32IMC/barrel-shifter configuration is not modeled; compressed and M-extension behavior is absent.
changes.concern: A property described as unchanged cannot be evaluated against the original parameterized core.

changes.title: Reset/regfile initialization changed
changes.analysis: Original only initializes cpuregs if REGS_INIT_ZERO is set; default REGS_INIT_ZERO=0. Candidate clears regfile to zero on every resetn low. Original reset block resets PC/control but not the register file.
changes.property_impact: Architectural state at reset differs; candidate can mask unconstrained register initial values and may make ADD operand cases easier.
changes.concern: This changes reset semantics outside the apparent target.

changes.title: rvfi_order never increments
changes.analysis: Original increments rvfi_order with rvfi_valid. Candidate only initializes rvfi_order to 0 and never assigns it in normal operation.
changes.property_impact: RVFI ordering is invalid; any checker relying on order sees a constant 0.
changes.concern: The narrow ADD check may not check order, but the RVFI interface is materially wrong.

changes.title: rvfi_valid asserted unconditionally in EXEC
changes.analysis: Original rvfi_valid depends on resetn, launch_next_insn or trap, and dbg_valid_insn. Candidate sets rvfi_valid<=1 in STATE_EXEC for every fetched instruction, including non-ADD instructions that it marks as traps.
changes.property_impact: Retirement timing and valid/trap qualification differ from the original wrapper contract. A random fetch can produce an RVFI record for a non-ADD instruction.
changes.concern: If the checker only samples CHECK_CYCLE, this may still be used to satisfy the ADD property without representing original retirement.

changes.title: rvfi_halt and trap semantics changed
changes.analysis: Original drives rvfi_halt from trap. Candidate only resets rvfi_halt and never assigns it in normal operation. Candidate also forces rvfi_trap=1 for every instruction other than the 32-bit ADD pattern, whereas original executes many legal non-ADD instructions.
changes.property_impact: Trap/halt reporting is not the original behavior; legal instruction sequences are misrepresented.
changes.concern: ADD-only target may hide this, but full-core RVFI behavior is lost.

changes.title: Instruction fetch accepts mem_ready without mem_valid
changes.analysis: Original memory transfer uses mem_valid && mem_ready. Candidate STATE_FETCH checks only if (mem_ready) before loading instr from mem_rdata. Concrete reachable sequence: reset releases, state=FETCH, mem_valid=0 before the edge, random mem_ready=1; candidate captures mem_rdata and enters EXEC, while original would not accept the transfer until mem_valid is asserted.
changes.property_impact: The memory handshake is violated and can inject a spurious fetch/RVFI record without a valid bus transaction.
changes.concern: The wrapper's mem_ready is a free random input, so this is reachable in the target environment.

changes.title: Loads, stores, and memory writes omitted
changes.analysis: Candidate look-ahead outputs are tied to 0, the state machine only fetches instructions, and there are no mem_do_rdata/mem_do_wdata paths. All non-ADD instructions, including loads/stores, become rvfi_trap=1.
changes.property_impact: RVFI mem fields are always zero and memory instructions cannot retire as in the original.
changes.concern: Target ADD check does not exercise this, but the core is not a general picorv32.

changes.title: PCPI/MUL/DIV modules stubbed
changes.analysis: Candidate pcpi_mul, fast_mul, and div all drive zero outputs and the core never asserts pcpi_valid. Original implements multiply/divide PCPI. The wrapper enables ENABLE_FAST_MUL and ENABLE_DIV.
changes.property_impact: M-extension instructions are not executed; RV32IMC behavior is not represented.
changes.concern: Other checks generated from checks.cfg would not be meaningful against this candidate.

changes.title: AXI/WB/regs modules replaced with stubs
changes.analysis: picorv32_regs returns zero and ignores writes; picorv32_axi, picorv32_axi_adapter, and picorv32_wb are tied off. Original implements these interfaces and adapters.
changes.property_impact: Other integration wrappers and memory interfaces are nonfunctional, even if the target wrapper does not instantiate them.
changes.concern: Changes outside the apparent target can break other checks or configurations.

changes.title: Compressed ISA support removed
changes.analysis: Wrapper sets COMPRESSED_ISA=1. Candidate ADD detection only recognizes the 32-bit R-type encoding and has no compressed decode; C.ADD and all other compressed instructions are trapped.
changes.property_impact: Compressed ADD cannot retire through the candidate as in the original wrapper.
changes.concern: The targeted insn_add check may only generate uncompressed ADD, but the configured core is RV32IMC.

changes.title: CSR RVFI behavior removed
changes.analysis: Original conditionally sets rvfi_csr_mcycle/minstret masks/data for CSR read instructions. Candidate only zeroes these outputs and never sets them based on rvfi_insn.
changes.property_impact: CSR-related RVFI checks are not represented.
changes.concern: The generated task defines RISCV_FORMAL_CSR_MCYCLE and RISCV_FORMAL_CSR_MINSTRET, so this is part of the formal environment even if the ADD check may not exercise it.

changes.title: Internal FORMAL assertions/restrictions removed
changes.analysis: Original contains `ifdef FORMAL restrictions/assertions, including memory-stall restrictions and look-ahead assertions. Candidate removes them.
changes.property_impact: Internal formal guards are gone; only the external insn_add_ch0 checker remains.
changes.concern: Frontend success does not replace removed formal assumptions/assertions.

changes.title: Candidate property claim conflicts with environment
changes.analysis: property_proposal.md says 'unchanged', while environment.md admits the core is replaced by a partial ADD-only model. The original check configuration is not unchanged.
changes.property_impact: A reviewer trusting the proposal would incorrectly believe the upstream property is being evaluated.
changes.concern: Treat property_proposal.md as a candidate claim, not upstream fact.

open_questions: Does insn_add_ch0.sby only sample at CHECK_CYCLE=20 (see original/upstream/insn_add_ch0.sby depth/skip and defines), so the candidate can satisfy the property by presenting one synthetic ADD RVFI record rather than executing the original ADD pipeline?
Can the candidate's `if (mem_ready)` fetch path (candidate/picorv32.v lines 219-228) accept random mem_rdata while mem_valid is low and thereby generate a spurious ADD record at the check cycle?

Because candidate zeroes regfile on reset (candidate/picorv32.v line 186) while original default REGS_INIT_ZERO=0 leaves registers unconstrained, does the candidate mask ADD operand cases that the original formal check would explore?
Does rvfi_insn_check ignore all RVFI records before CHECK_CYCLE, making candidate's forced traps for non-ADD instructions before the check cycle irrelevant to PASS?
Would the checker still pass if rvfi_order remains constant 0 and rvfi_valid is asserted unconditionally in STATE_EXEC (candidate/picorv32.v lines 230-234)?
Are the stubbed picorv32_regs/pcpi_mul/fast_mul/div/axi/wb modules (candidate/picorv32.v lines 256-560) expected to matter for the target task or only for other checks/configurations?
Does the target environment define RISCV_FORMAL_CSR_MISA or other CSR macros that would make the removed CSR logic or ADD misa check relevant?
